why: Voice is a COMBAT-LEGIBILITY channel, not decoration. The property being optimised is SEPARATION: can a player tell by ear alone WHICH champion just acted, without looking. This file is the measured baseline of the shipped 2-voice pack plus the calibration that defines the pass/fail threshold.

instrument.features: torchaudio kaldi fbank, 80 mel bins, dither=0, 16 kHz, per-utterance mean-normalised (identical to CosyVoiceFrontEnd._extract_spk_embedding)
instrument.prosody: librosa pyin F0 (55-800 Hz), spectral centroid/rolloff/flatness/tilt, onset rate, RMS dynamics
instrument.audio: all sources transcoded to 16 kHz mono via ffmpeg before analysis

calibration.corpus: data/blizzard-overlay/sounds -- Blizzard WC3 hero soundsets, clips >= 1.2s, soundsets with >= 4 such clips
calibration.rationale: A shipped, professionally cast arena roster is the empirical definition of 'you can tell who spoke'. It supplies both a same-speaker and a different-speaker distribution on the SAME instrument and the SAME kind of material (short, shouted, dry game VO), so the threshold is derived rather than asserted.
calibration.provenance: Blizzard-owned audio, local-only overlay, used here as a measuring reference only -- never shipped or redistributed as part of this analysis.

confusable.meaning: At cos >= 0.50 the measured likelihood ratio p(s|same speaker)/p(s|different speaker) crosses 1.0 -- the instrument can no longer assert the two clips came from different people. Treat any champion pair at or above this as a legibility defect.
confusable.derivedFrom: likelihood-ratio crossover of the WC3 same/different-actor distributions (LR=1 at cos 0.49); rounded up to 0.50, where 17.6% of genuinely-different WC3 actor pairs still land.

target.meaning: Design goal for a NEWLY cast pair. 0.40 is the WC3 different-actor p60 and sits at LR=0.44 (about 2:1 in favour of 'different speaker'). Casting to 0.40 leaves headroom for the fact that a single 1-4s clip is a noisy measurement.

pairBudget.meaning: Even a professionally cast roster is not all-pairs clean: 17.6% of WC3 different-actor pairs exceed 0.50. Demanding 0% is not achievable with this instrument. The roster passes when its over-threshold fraction is at or below the WC3 control.

f0Register.meaning: campplus is nearly blind to pitch register (corr of embedding distance with |dF0| over WC3 actor pairs = +0.09), yet register is one of the strongest cues a listener uses mid-fight. Gate on it SEPARATELY: no two champions likely to share an arena should sit within 2 semitones of each other's median F0 unless their embedding cosine is already below the target.
f0Register.derivedFrom: WC3 actors span 46.3 semitones with only 5.2% of pairs inside 1 semitone; the shipped GGD roster spans 16.1 semitones with 20.3% of pairs inside 1 semitone.

baseline.duplicateNote: 19 champion ids ship a byte-identical copy of another id's clip (same character duplicated across hero numbers, cf. task #113). Collapsed to one representative before every statistic below so duplicates do not flatter or inflate the result.

monteCarlo12.meaning: expected confusable pairs (cos >= 0.478) among the 66 pairs formed by 12 combatants drawn at random

systemVoiceCeiling.meaning: All 11 macOS ja_JP system voices rendered on identical lines collapse to 4 mutually distinguishable identities at the confusable threshold. Casting more system voices does NOT solve this; reference-cloned voices are required.

controllableViaReferenceClip.note: the primary thing a zero-shot reference clip transfers; this is what the threshold gates
transfers with the reference speaker; measurable per clip and near-orthogonal to campplus, so it must be gated separately
the strongest prosodic correlate of embedding distance measured here (r=+0.26); controllable by both reference tempo and line length
reference-driven; also the axis most polluted by codec and loudness normalisation, so measure post-normalisation
growl vs clean vs breathy; transfers from the reference but weakly and inconsistently

notControllableViaReferenceClip.note: a shout vs a mutter is set by the line and the engine's instruct channel, not by the speaker embedding. Two champions on the same reference voice can be pushed apart by delivery, but this analysis cannot measure that from a single neutral clip.
the pack is EBU R128 normalised to -16 LUFS by design, which deliberately destroys this axis. It is a mixing decision, not a casting one.
a real separation lever in the mix, entirely outside the TTS reference clip. Out of scope for casting; worth noting as headroom the audio layer still has.

the single strongest real-world cue and the reason the owner asks for source-character references -- a familiar voice plus a familiar line is placed instantly. Not measurable by any acoustic distance; it lives in quotes.json 'character' and 'source'.

prosodyVsEmbeddingCorrelations.note: correlation of campplus distance with each prosodic gap, over WC3 actor pairs. All are weak, which is the actionable finding: an embedding-only gate under-weights cues listeners rely on, especially pitch.
